title: Admin policy, never-rules and safety vocabulary
owns: app/main/admin.ts, app/main/policy/** (except the audit write path, which lifecycle owns), the audit-retention call in main.ts (small hunk)

findings.title: A broken or too-new admin policy makes Ember delete every audit record older than 30 days
findings.scenario: An organisation keeps audit logs for a year (auditRetentionDays: 365). One host's policy.json gets a typo, or a staged rollout reaches an older Ember that reads the new keys as a mistake (docs say this locks Ember down). On the next start admin.ts uses LOCKDOWN, which has no auditRetentionDays, and main.ts runs audit.prune(policy.auditRetentionDays ?? 30). Every monthly audit file older than 30 days is rm'ed, irreversibly, exactly when the administrator's intent can't be read.
findings.evidence: Script (scratchpad e2.ts): files audit-2026-01, -05, -08, -10 in a dir, now = 2026-10-27. parseAdminPolicy({auditRetentionDays:365, futureKey:1}) returned error 'Unrecognized key' with retention undefined. After prune(retention ?? 30) only audit-2026-10.jsonl was left; with the valid policy (365) Jan, May and Aug would stay. The only use of admin.error besides display is a log line (main.ts:245).
findings.fix: Do not prune while admin.error is set (a locked-down Ember should never delete evidence), or keep the largest retention ever seen in a sidecar file. Document that a broken policy never prunes.

findings.title: Lockdown still connects the brain to GitHub Copilot and forgets the organisation's provider (BYOK) and never-look list
findings.scenario: The organisation requires its own model endpoint ('provider': Ember then never uses a GitHub sign-in) and bans windows with neverLook. The policy is broken (typo, or a newer key on an older Ember, which is documented to lock down). LOCKDOWN turns off actions, voice, desk, screen images and commands but carries no provider and no neverLook. admin.error is only logged and shown in settings, so startBrain resolves a GitHub token (own sign-in, GH CLI or environment) and connects to Copilot. The conductor's describe_screen still reads the focused window, because features.actions=false only stops tasks starting, and the admin's never-look entries are not applied. Screen text the organisation wanted kept in-house goes to github.com. Docs promise only 'no actions, no listening', but the BYOK text says GitHub is never used.
findings.evidence: Lockdown policy from a broken file: provider undefined, neverLook [] (scratchpad e2 and e11). main.ts:1307 builds the provider only from policy.provider; line 1558 'provider ? null : resolveToken(...)'. grep shows admin.error is read only at main.ts:245 and 369. startTask refuses on actions=false (host.ts:974) but conductor tools describe_screen and show_me are unaffected.
findings.fix: While admin.error is set, do not start the brain (or start it only after an explicit user acknowledgement), and do not run describe_screen. At minimum state in docs and settings that a broken policy sends screen text to GitHub, and keep the last-good provider/neverLook values.

findings.title: Windows 'never run programs' rules (Run dialog, Explorer address box, Open/Run-as commands) only match a few display languages
findings.scenario: A Windows 11 user in Russian, Polish, Turkish, Swedish, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Greek, Ukrainian, Hebrew or Arabic (all unlisted) has given Ember a File Explorer grant. Their Run dialog (title 'Выполнить', box 'Открыть:') and Explorer's address box ('Адрес', 'Adress', 'Adresa', 'Osoite', 'Cím') are not recognised, so type_text of `cmd` or `powershell -c ...` into them is allowed with no question. The Enter or OK that runs it is asked, but the question never says a program will start. The same localized lists decide the Open/Run-as-administrator command labels, so none of the never-rules that exist for English apply.
findings.evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e5, os win32, explorer grant): type 'cmd' into the Run box was deny for en, de, pt, zh-TW, ko, ja and allow ('Ember may act in Explorer') for ru, pl, tr, sv, cs, da, fi, hu, el, uk, he, ar. Address box was deny for en, tr, da, nl, pl, pt and allow for ru, sv, cs, fi, hu, he, ar, el, uk. READ_ONLY_WINDOW title list (vocabulary.ts:249), RUN_BOX (:211) and ADDRESS_BOX (:209) hold only en/de/fr/es/it/pt/nl/ja/zh/ko. The localized strings in the test are from memory; the point is that none of those languages appear in the regexes. Only English Windows is verified by win32-vocabulary CI.
findings.fix: Key the rules off language-independent facts (explorer.exe + dialog class #32770 + the combo's AutomationId or ClassName, the address band's AutomationId) from the UIA bridge, or add the missing Windows display languages and test each one on a localized runner.

findings.title: Explorer 'never open programs or scripts' does nothing while Explorer hides known extensions (the default)
findings.platforms: windows (macOS Finder has no equivalent rule)
findings.scenario: Windows hides extensions of registered file types by default, so setup.exe, install.bat, run.cmd, setup.msi show as 'setup', 'install', 'run'. opensProgram() decides by the item's name ending in .exe/.bat/..., so an Enter or open on such an item is 'any other item'. The user sees only 'Borrow your keyboard to press Enter on “setup” list item in Explorer?' and approving it starts the program with no further dialog (unless the file carries a web mark and the English-only 'Open File - Security Warning' check applies). The same applies to a click that activates the item.
findings.evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e9, os win32, explorer grant): `Enter` on 'setup.exe' / 'install.bat' / 'run.cmd' / 'payload.ps1' = deny; the same keys on 'setup', 'install', 'run' = confirm with the generic 'Ember needs your mouse or keyboard' reason (and a click on 'setup' = allow). The limitation is stated only in a code comment (vocabulary.ts:274-281: 'such an item is judged as any other'). OPENS_PROGRAMS.darwin is empty, so Finder .app/.command items open the same way.
findings.fix: Have the UIA bridge pass the item's ItemType ('Application', 'Windows Batch File', ...) or read the Type column, and refuse Enter and open clicks on those; failing that, refuse Enter on any Explorer item with no extension that isn't a known folder. Document the gap until fixed.

findings.title: Settings that weaken protection or grant device access go through unasked once the Settings app is allowed (GNOME, Windows, macOS)
findings.area: tiers: security settings are 'Never' in PLAN §5
findings.scenario: After one 'Allow' (or 'Always in Settings'), a task in GNOME Settings, Windows Settings or System Settings can flip Automatic Screen Lock, Lock Screen on Suspend, Location Services, Camera, Microphone, Developer Mode, 'Allow Remote Assistance', macOS Camera/Microphone/Photos/Contacts/Bluetooth app toggles or Login Items without a question. A toggle is judged only by its own label's word stems (SECURITY_STEMS) or by an enclosing dialog's wording. App-name toggles ('Terminal' in macOS Camera) and these labels match no stem, and a settings page isn't a dialog. A page-injected goal such as 'turn off the screen lock' is therefore silent.
findings.evidence: Engine runs (scratchpad e8, e7, e15). Linux gnome-control-center with an 'act' grant: switches Location Services, Camera, Microphone, Automatic Screen Lock, Lock Screen on Suspend, Automatic Login all 'allow' (Screen Sharing, Remote Login, File Sharing 'confirm'). macOS System Settings: toggle 'Terminal' in panes Camera, Microphone, Location Services, Photos, Contacts, Files & Folders, Local Network, Bluetooth, Login Items & Extensions, Sharing = allow; only Privacy & Security, Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring, Full Disk Access, Automation are denied (SECURITY_TITLE.darwin, vocabulary.ts:75). Windows SystemSettings: Camera access, Microphone access, Location services, Developer Mode, 'Allow Remote Assistance...' = allow (Remote Desktop and Sign-in options ask). macOS pane titles are assumed to be the window title.
findings.fix: Treat the Settings apps of each OS (gnome-control-center, SystemSettings, System Settings) as 'security-sensitive': ask for every toggle, or add the missing stems (screen lock, lock screen, location, camera, microphone, developer mode, remote assistance, login/startup items) and the remaining macOS privacy pane titles.

findings.title: The administrator's policy is read once at start on the PC (and a fixed policy isn't picked up either)
findings.scenario: IT disables actions or SSH, adds a never-look entry, or repairs a broken policy. Ember is an autostarted, long-running agent and keeps the snapshot loaded at start; a locked-down Ember stays locked down after the file is fixed, and a running Ember keeps acting after a tightening. The remote helper re-reads every 10 s (app/remote/admin.ts POLICY_EVERY_MS), so the two sides behave differently. No document says a restart is needed.
findings.evidence: grep: adminPolicy.load is called only at main.ts:210 (doctor) and 244 (start); PolicyWatch is used only under app/remote. PolicyEngine, TargetsRuntime and SettingsStore all close over the one `admin` object.
findings.fix: Poll the policy source (mtime for the file, registry value) every 10 s like the remote does and rebuild the engine inputs, or state 'restart Ember after changing the policy' in DEVELOPING.md §5/§10.7/§11.7 and the settings window.

findings.title: The administrator's confirmEveryAction does not apply to commands
findings.scenario: An administrator sets confirmEveryAction: true ('A click before every action, every time') and commands.local: 'on'. Ordinary commands then run with no question, because decideCommand's policyAsk looks only at privileged, commands mode 'ask', the user's ask-every, taint and carried text. The GUI engine honours confirmEveryAction (policy.ts:1821). The docs list it only for GUI actions.
findings.evidence: grep confirmEveryAction: used by PolicyEngine wiring only (main.ts:1416, targets/runtime.ts:1135, desktop-child.ts); not in local-service.ts, wsl-service.ts, remote-service.ts or flow.ts. decideCommand(...) for `ls` with mode 'on' returns 'run' (corpus defaults).
findings.fix: Pass admin.confirmEveryAction into the command service and treat it as mode 'ask' (stricter-of), or document that only commands.* controls commands.

findings.title: The Linux 'run or display' dialog and 'allow executing file as program' rules cover only en/de/fr/es/it/pt
findings.area: never-rules: running programs from the file manager
findings.scenario: On RHEL in Russian, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Polish or Dutch, Nautilus's 'Run' button and Properties' 'Allow executing file as program' check box are not recognised. A task with a Files grant can tick the execute bit without a question, and clicking the dialog's Run button is likewise unasked (Enter on the file is still asked, but generically). Reaching the dialog needs a non-default Nautilus setting (executable-text-activation = ask).
findings.evidence: Engine run (scratchpad e6, os linux, nautilus grant): Run button in en and fr = deny; ru 'Запустить', ja '実行', zh '运行', ko '실행', pl, nl = allow. Check box 'Allow executing file as program' = deny, but the ru, ja, zh, ko, pl, nl equivalents = allow. RUN_WORDS/RUN_FILE_DIALOG/RUN_ANSWER (policy.ts:738-754) list six languages, while RISKY_WORDS covers 16. The translated strings in the test are from memory.
findings.fix: Extend RUNS_PROGRAM, RUN_FILE_DIALOG, RUN_ANSWER and RUN_WORDS to the same languages as RISKY_WORDS (take Nautilus 3.28's .po files), or match on the button's role plus the dialog's structure instead of words.

findings.title: Non-Latin keysym names bypass the 'system keys' never-rule on Linux with a multi-layout keyboard
findings.scenario: With a us,ru (or us,gr, us,ua...) keyboard, a task calls press_keys 'ctrl+alt+Cyrillic_ie'. isSystemKey tests the key name against Latin letters only, so it is allowed to ask. Ember's borrow resolves the keysym through the other layout group to the physical T key and presses Ctrl+Alt+T, which opens a terminal in GNOME. Cyrillic_en lands on the physical key of Ember's own Allow chord Ctrl+Alt+Y (the Confirmer's blocked() check, driving, makes that harmless in practice). The user must still click Allow on 'Press Ctrl+Alt+Cyrillic Ie', so the impact is small, but it is a bypass of the stated 'terminals and Ember's own shortcuts are for the user only' rule. Windows and macOS refuse by modifier family.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad e1: canonicalKeys/isSystemKey for ctrl+alt+Cyrillic_ie, Greek_tau, Cyrillic_en, Hebrew_alef all false and decide() = confirm; ctrl+alt+t and ctrl+alt+y = deny. Scratchpad e13 with a us,ru layout: shortcutStroke(Cyrillic_ie) = keycode 28, the same key as Latin t (hands/keymap.ts:60-66 searches layout.others).
findings.fix: On Linux treat any chord containing both ctrl and alt as a system key unless its key is in the safe/navigation list, or resolve the keysym to its physical keycode and judge the Latin name of that keycode; also refuse non-ASCII keysym names with ctrl or alt.

findings.title: Confirmation text can be spoofed with quote characters and shows only the first 59 characters of typed text
findings.scenario: quote() wraps screen-supplied names and the model's typed text in “ ” without escaping, so a page can name a button `Close” button in Firefox? Nothing is sent. Delete` and the question reads `Click “Close” button in Firefox? Nothing is sent. Delete” push button in Firefox? ...`, which imitates Ember's own sentence. A cursor_text question shows a long text only as its first ~59 characters ('type “Hi there, thanks for the update on the quarterly figures, s…” into ...'), with no length, so the tail the user approves can't be seen. Risky-but-unasked steps still get the 'You didn't ask for this' line.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad e3: prompts printed exactly as quoted above; the long text was cut at 59 characters with only an ellipsis.
findings.fix: Replace “ and ” (and newlines) inside quote(); add the character count for text longer than the cut ('…, 124 characters'); show the full text in the card for typed text over a few hundred characters.

findings.title: Remote-desktop and VM viewers are not remote surfaces on Linux and macOS
findings.scenario: REMOTE_SURFACE is null off Windows, so Remmina, virt-manager/virt-viewer, GNOME Boxes, vncviewer, Screen Sharing, UTM, Parallels and the like are ordinary apps. A task with a grant can use the borrowed keyboard or mouse on a viewer showing a terminal or polkit prompt of another machine; the terminal, security-window and never-look checks can't see inside, exactly the reasoning given for Windows. Every borrowed step still asks, but 'Ember never types into terminals' can be sidestepped. The sample admin policy lists Remmina in neverLook, so admins already know the gap.
findings.evidence: vocabulary and remote-surface.ts:31-35; DEVELOPING.md §10.8 says 'Other remote viewers ... aren't covered yet ... Linux and macOS are unaffected' without mentioning virt-manager or Remmina on RHEL.
findings.fix: Add a Linux and macOS REMOTE_SURFACE row (remmina, virt-manager, virt-viewer, gnome-boxes, vinagre, krdc, vncviewer, x2goclient, anydesk, teamviewer; Screen Sharing, UTM, Parallels, VMware, VirtualBox, Windows App) or add them to the default never-look list, and document it.

findings.title: PLAN §5 promises confirmation for new domains and downloads, and admin 'domains'; neither exists
findings.scenario: The frozen safety table lists 'new domain; uploads/downloads' as Confirm tier and M8.7 lists admin 'domains'. In the code a granted browser navigates and downloads unasked, and the admin schema has no domain key.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad e14: click 'Download' button = allow; typing a URL into the address bar = allow; link to another site = allow. AdminPolicySchema (admin.ts:29) has no domains key.
findings.fix: Implement or update PLAN.md and the release notes so an administrator doesn't expect them.

findings.title: Default never-look entries 'keeper' (Windows) and 'seahorse' (Linux) are common words matched as substrings of window titles
findings.scenario: isNeverLook matches case-insensitive substrings of '<app> <title>'. A browser tab titled 'Housekeeper wanted' or 'Seahorse facts' is treated as private: Ember refuses to read or act in that window with 'This window is private'.
findings.fix: Match the default entries against the app name or window class only (not the title), or use word-boundary matching.

findings.title: A UTF-8 byte-order mark makes a correct policy.json lock Ember down with a misleading message
findings.scenario: An administrator saves policy.json from an editor that adds a BOM. Ember locks down and says 'p is not valid JSON: Unexpected token ...', though the file looks valid. The strict schema also locks down on a '$schema' or '_comment' key.
findings.evidence: Scratchpad e11: parseAdminPolicy('﻿{}') returned the lockdown with that message.
findings.fix: Strip a leading U+FEFF before JSON.parse and mention unknown keys by name in the settings notice.

findings.title: Consent cards say text goes to GitHub Copilot even when the organisation's own provider is in use
findings.scenario: For an organisation with a BYOK provider the WSL, commands and SSH cards (and their copies in app/renderer/prompt/copy.ts:173,201,215) tell the user that what Ember reads goes to GitHub Copilot. The sha256 the user's yes carries covers that wrong sentence.
findings.evidence: Hardcoded strings at consent.ts:35, 67, 128; settings page (renderer/home/main.ts:315) correctly says 'your organisation's model service'.
findings.fix: Build the card text from the provider state ('your organisation's model service').

findings.title: The 'Stopped' bubble appears at once and never mentions parts that were late
findings.scenario: stopEverything calls `void killSwitch.pull(source)` and shows 'Okay, I've stopped everything.' immediately; the returned `late` list (parts still winding down, e.g. a command in its 1 s SIGKILL ladder or a slow remote link) is only logged.
findings.evidence: main.ts:803-811; killswitch.ts returns {ms, late}; run/kill.ts LADDER_MS term 300, kill 1000, last 1500.
findings.fix: Await pull() briefly and add 'Still stopping: build-01…' to the bubble when late is not empty.
